sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Arkansas, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Tuesday, October 27Passed

By mail, email or fax: your application must reach the county clerk by Tuesday, October 27, 2026 (7 days before the election). In person or by a designated bearer: by the close of business on Friday, October 30, 2026. For a patient in a hospital or care facility, an authorized agent can apply until 1:30 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

By mail: received by the county clerk by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. In person (by you or your designated bearer): by the close of business on Friday, October 30, 2026. Faxed or emailed ballots are not accepted (except as allowed for military and overseas voters). (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Monday, November 2, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Arkansas’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Arkansas or in another state? What Arkansas says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Yes, you need a reason. The Secretary of State's page lists these: you will be unavoidably absent from your polling place on Election Day; you cannot go because of illness or physical disability; you are a member of the uniformed services or merchant marine, or their spouse or dependent, away because of active duty; or you are an Arkansas resident living outside the United States for a while. The state's application form also lists living in a licensed long-term care or residential care facility and a religious observance or holiday. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Download the state's absentee ballot application, fill in all six sections, sign and date it, and mail it to the county clerk where you are registered. You can also ask your county clerk to mail you a blank application. If you live outside the county where you are registered (a student at school in another county, for example), the application lets you ask for ballots for every election through December 31, and the clerk then mails them automatically. Open it (official page)
  • Email or fax. You may send the signed application to your county clerk by email or fax. (Only military and overseas voters can get the ballot itself by email.) Open it (official page)
  • In person. Hand the application to your county clerk yourself, or have a person you choose (a "designated bearer") take it. A designated bearer can handle ballots for no more than two voters per election, must show photo ID and sign the clerk's register. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it to your county clerk so it arrives by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)
  • In person. Bring it to the county clerk's office yourself, or send it with your designated bearer, by the close of business on Friday, October 30, 2026. You cannot hand it in at a polling place. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Put a copy of a photo ID in the return envelope with your ballot. It must show your name and picture and be no more than four years past its expiration date. If the copy is missing, your ballot is treated as a provisional ballot. Fill in and sign the voter statement that comes with the ballot; a ballot without it is rejected. Active-duty service members and their dependents away on duty do not need to send ID; residents of a licensed care facility may send a form signed by the facility's administrator instead. If someone helped you fill out the application, they print and sign their name and address on it. No witness or notary is needed. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Arkansas’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Monday, October 19, 2026 to Monday, November 2, 2026.

Early voting runs from Monday, October 19, 2026 through Monday, November 2, 2026: 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Friday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Saturday, and it ends at 5 p.m. on Monday, November 2. Check your county for places. (official page)

Students

At school in Arkansas, away from home

The Secretary of State's answer for students: a student may be considered a resident of the place they lived before becoming a student, or may register at school if they mean to make it home. A student may not be registered or vote in more than one place. (official page)

At school in another state, with Arkansas as home

The state's pages do not speak to out-of-state students separately. Its general rule is the same as for students in Arkansas: you may keep your residence where you lived before becoming a student, and you may be registered in only one place. A student at school in another state who keeps an Arkansas registration can apply to vote absentee as someone who will be away on Election Day. (official page)

Military and overseas

Uniformed service members, merchant marines, their spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living outside the country can register and ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application (it must be mailed) and can get the ballot by email. They must vote by Election Day, and the ballot must reach the county clerk by 5 p.m. on Friday, November 13, 2026 (10 days after the election). Active-duty members and dependents do not need to send ID. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is a backup if your ballot does not come in time. (federal guide)

Arkansas in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The deadline to deliver a voted absentee ballot in person is the Friday before the election (October 30, 2026), not Election Day. After that, the ballot must come by mail and arrive by 7:30 p.m. on November 3.
  • Arkansas polls are open 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. on Election Day.
  • The photo ID rule here comes from the State Board of Election Commissioners' training for county election boards (prepared for 2024). The Secretary of State's absentee page does not repeat it; ask your county clerk if you are unsure what to enclose.
  • Voters who live outside their county, have a disability, or live in a licensed care facility can ask for ballots for every election in one calendar year; the county clerk mails those ballots automatically at least 25 days before each election.
  • A general runoff, where one is needed, is on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.
